What Is Rectal Prolapse?

Rectal prolapse is a condition where the rectum, which is the lower part of the large intestine, slips from its normal position and protrudes through the anal opening.

The rectum is normally supported by muscles and tissues in the pelvic floor. When these supporting structures become weak, the rectum may start moving downward.

Rectal prolapse can appear in different forms:

Complete Rectal Prolapse

In complete rectal prolapse, the full thickness of the rectal wall comes out through the anus. It may be visible during bowel movements or even while standing or walking in advanced cases.

Partial Rectal Prolapse

In partial prolapse, only the inner lining of the rectum protrudes outward. This may sometimes be confused with hemorrhoids because both conditions can cause tissue coming out of the anus.

Internal Rectal Prolapse

In internal prolapse, the rectum folds inside itself but does not come outside the anus. It may cause difficulty passing stool or a feeling of incomplete bowel emptying.

Can Hysterectomy Cause Rectal Prolapse?

A hysterectomy does not directly cause rectal prolapse in every woman. However, changes in pelvic anatomy after surgery may contribute to weakening of the support structures that hold pelvic organs in place.

The pelvic organs, including the bladder, uterus, rectum, and vagina, are supported by a network of muscles, ligaments, and connective tissues. When one supporting structure changes, it can sometimes affect the balance of the pelvic floor.

After hysterectomy, some women may develop pelvic organ prolapse after hysterectomy, which can involve different pelvic organs, including the rectum.

Factors that may increase the risk include:

  • Weak pelvic floor muscles
  • Previous pelvic surgeries
  • Age-related tissue changes
  • Chronic constipation and repeated straining
  • Long-term coughing
  • Heavy lifting
  • Obesity
  • Conditions affecting connective tissues

It is important to remember that symptoms can vary from person to person. A proper medical evaluation is needed to identify the exact cause.

Why Does Rectal Prolapse Happen After Hysterectomy?

The pelvic floor works like a supportive structure that helps maintain the position of pelvic organs. After hysterectomy, some women may experience changes in this support system.

Weakening of Pelvic Support Tissues

The uterus provides part of the natural support within the pelvis. After its removal, surrounding tissues may experience changes over time, especially if there are existing weaknesses in pelvic muscles or ligaments.

Existing Pelvic Floor Weakness

Some women may already have weakened pelvic floor muscles due to childbirth, ageing, or previous strain. Hysterectomy may reveal or contribute to symptoms that were not noticeable earlier.

Chronic Pressure on the Pelvic Floor

Repeated pressure inside the abdomen can place stress on pelvic support structures.

Common causes include:

  • Long-term constipation
  • Frequent straining during bowel movements
  • Chronic respiratory conditions causing repeated coughing
  • Heavy physical activities involving lifting

Symptoms of Rectal Prolapse After Hysterectomy

The symptoms of rectal prolapse can develop gradually. Some women may initially notice mild changes that become more noticeable over time.

Common symptoms include:

  • A bulge or tissue coming out of the anus
  • A feeling of pressure or fullness in the rectal area
  • Difficulty completing bowel movements
  • The need to push or manually assist stool passage
  • Mucus discharge from the anus
  • Rectal discomfort or irritation
  • Bleeding in some cases
  • Feeling that the bowel has not completely emptied

One common concern among women is confusing rectal prolapse vs hemorrhoids.

While hemorrhoids are swollen blood vessels around the anus, rectal prolapse involves the movement of rectal tissue outside its normal position. A specialist examination can help differentiate between these conditions.

When Should You See a Doctor?

Many women delay seeking medical advice because they feel embarrassed discussing symptoms related to bowel movements. However, early evaluation can help prevent worsening of the condition.

You should consider consulting a specialist if you experience:

  • Tissue coming out of the anus during bowel movements
  • Increasing difficulty passing stool
  • Persistent pelvic pressure or discomfort
  • Bleeding or mucus discharge
  • Symptoms affecting daily activities

A proctology specialist can assess the severity of the prolapse and recommend the most suitable treatment approach.

At Chirag Global Hospitals, Bangalore, patients can receive a detailed evaluation for rectal prolapse and related colorectal conditions with personalised treatment planning.

How Is Rectal Prolapse Diagnosed?

Diagnosis usually begins with a detailed discussion about symptoms and medical history, including previous surgeries such as hysterectomy.

A doctor may perform:

Physical Examination

A clinical examination helps identify whether rectal tissue is protruding and assess the severity of the condition.

Digital Rectal Examination

This helps evaluate muscle strength and rectal function.

Additional Tests

Depending on symptoms, doctors may recommend tests such as:

  • Colonoscopy to examine the inside of the colon
  • Defecography to study bowel movement patterns
  • Anorectal manometry to assess rectal muscle function
  • Imaging tests to evaluate pelvic structures

The goal of diagnosis is not only to confirm rectal prolapse but also to understand the underlying causes and plan appropriate treatment.

Treatment Options for Rectal Prolapse After Hysterectomy

The treatment for rectal prolapse after hysterectomy depends on factors such as the severity of prolapse, symptoms, overall health, and whether the prolapse is affecting daily life.

Mild cases may be managed with lifestyle changes and pelvic floor strengthening, while more advanced cases may require surgical treatment.

Non-Surgical Management

For early or mild symptoms, doctors may recommend steps to reduce pressure on the pelvic floor.

These may include:

  • Increasing fibre intake to prevent constipation
  • Drinking adequate fluids
  • Avoiding excessive straining during bowel movements
  • Pelvic floor muscle exercises
  • Maintaining a healthy weight
  • Managing chronic cough or conditions that increase abdominal pressure

These measures may help improve symptoms but may not correct a significant rectal prolapse.

Surgical Treatment for Rectal Prolapse

When rectal prolapse is significant or continues to worsen, surgery may be recommended. The aim of surgery is to restore the normal position of the rectum and improve bowel function.

Treatment options may include:

Rectopexy

Rectopexy is a commonly performed procedure where the rectum is repositioned and secured inside the pelvis to prevent it from slipping down again.

It can be performed using minimally invasive techniques in suitable patients.

Perineal Procedures

Some procedures are performed through the area around the anus and may be considered depending on the patient’s condition, age, and health status.

Minimally Invasive Approaches

Laparoscopic or robotic-assisted techniques may be recommended in selected cases. These approaches may offer benefits such as smaller incisions and faster recovery for suitable patients.

The best treatment option is decided after a complete evaluation by a colorectal or proctology specialist.

Recovery After Rectal Prolapse Surgery

Recovery time after rectal prolapse surgery can vary depending on the procedure performed and individual health factors.

General recovery recommendations may include:

  • Following prescribed medications
  • Maintaining soft bowel movements
  • Avoiding heavy lifting during recovery
  • Following dietary recommendations
  • Attending follow-up appointments

Patients are usually advised to prevent constipation and avoid activities that place excessive pressure on the pelvic floor during healing.

Can Rectal Prolapse Be Prevented After Hysterectomy?

While rectal prolapse cannot always be completely prevented, maintaining pelvic floor health can reduce risk factors and support better bowel function.

Helpful habits include:

  • Eating a fibre-rich diet
  • Treating constipation early
  • Avoiding prolonged straining during bowel movements
  • Practising pelvic floor exercises as advised
  • Maintaining a healthy body weight
  • Staying physically active

Women who have undergone hysterectomy and notice pelvic or bowel-related changes should discuss these concerns with a healthcare professional.

Understanding the Link Between Hysterectomy and Pelvic Floor Health

A hysterectomy can improve quality of life for many women by treating conditions affecting the uterus. However, pelvic health involves a connected system of muscles and tissues that support multiple organs.

After hysterectomy, some women may experience conditions such as:

  • Rectocele (bulging of the rectal wall into the vaginal area)
  • Vaginal vault prolapse
  • Bladder prolapse (cystocele)
  • Rectal prolapse

Recognising symptoms early allows appropriate treatment before they significantly affect comfort and daily activities.

Frequently Asked Questions About Rectal Prolapse After Hysterectomy

Can hysterectomy cause rectal prolapse?

Hysterectomy does not directly cause rectal prolapse in every woman. However, changes in pelvic support after surgery may contribute to pelvic floor weakness, which can increase the risk of prolapse in some individuals.

What are the first signs of rectal prolapse after hysterectomy?

Early signs may include pelvic pressure, difficulty passing stool, incomplete bowel emptying, or a feeling that something is coming out of the anus during bowel movements.

Is rectal prolapse common in older women after hysterectomy?

Rectal prolapse is more commonly seen in older women because pelvic muscles and connective tissues can weaken with age. However, it can occur in younger women as well, especially with risk factors such as previous surgeries, childbirth, or chronic constipation.

How is rectal prolapse different from hemorrhoids?

Hemorrhoids are swollen veins around the anus, while rectal prolapse occurs when part of the rectum moves outside its normal position. The symptoms may overlap, so a medical examination is needed for accurate diagnosis.

Can rectal prolapse heal without surgery?

Small or mild prolapses may be managed with lifestyle changes and pelvic floor exercises. However, surgery is often required for complete rectal prolapse to restore normal anatomy.

What type of doctor treats rectal prolapse?

A colorectal surgeon or proctology specialist evaluates and treats rectal prolapse. They can recommend appropriate treatment based on symptoms and the severity of the condition.

When should I seek medical help for rectal prolapse?

You should consult a specialist if you notice tissue coming out of the anus, difficulty passing stool, bleeding, increasing discomfort, or symptoms affecting your daily activities.

Understanding the difference between ordinary fatigue and fatigue linked with colon cancer can help people recognise warning signs earlier. What Is Colon Cancer Fatigue?

Cancer-related fatigue is a common symptom experienced by many people with cancer, including colorectal cancer. It is not simply feeling sleepy or exhausted after physical work. Instead, it is often described as a deep lack of energy that affects concentration, motivation, and daily routines.

Unlike normal tiredness, colon cancer fatigue may:

  • Continue for days or weeks
  • Occur even after proper sleep
  • Make simple activities feel difficult
  • Affect work, exercise, and personal responsibilities
  • Be accompanied by other symptoms such as weight changes or digestive problems

Fatigue itself does not mean someone has colon cancer. However, persistent unexplained fatigue should be discussed with a healthcare professional, especially when combined with other warning signs.

Why Does Colon Cancer Cause Fatigue?

Several factors can contribute to fatigue in people with colon cancer. The cause may vary depending on the stage of cancer, overall health, and treatment status.

Blood Loss and Iron Deficiency Anaemia

One of the common reasons for fatigue in colon cancer is slow blood loss from the tumour.

Sometimes colon cancers can bleed internally in small amounts that are not visible. Over time, this can reduce iron levels and lead to iron deficiency anaemia.

When the body has fewer healthy red blood cells, less oxygen reaches tissues and organs. This can result in:

  • Constant tiredness
  • Weakness
  • Shortness of breath during activity
  • Dizziness
  • Pale skin
  • Reduced energy levels

Anaemia can sometimes be one of the early signs that leads doctors to investigate possible digestive tract problems.

The Body’s Immune Response to Cancer

Cancer can trigger inflammation inside the body. The immune system releases certain substances to fight abnormal cells, but these inflammatory changes can also affect normal body functions.

This ongoing response may cause:

  • Low energy levels
  • Reduced appetite
  • Muscle weakness
  • Feeling exhausted without a clear reason

This type of fatigue is not always relieved by rest because it is connected to internal changes happening in the body.

Increased Energy Demand of Cancer Cells

Cancer cells grow and multiply rapidly. This process requires energy and can affect how the body uses nutrients.

As cancer progresses, some people may experience:

  • Unintentional weight loss
  • Loss of appetite
  • Muscle loss
  • General weakness

These changes can contribute to ongoing tiredness and reduced physical strength.

Colon Cancer Treatment-Related Fatigue

For people undergoing colon cancer treatment, fatigue can also occur due to:

  • Chemotherapy
  • Radiation therapy
  • Surgery recovery
  • Changes in appetite and nutrition
  • Emotional stress

Treatment-related fatigue can continue even after treatment sessions because the body needs time to repair healthy tissues and recover.

How Is Colon Cancer Fatigue Different From Normal Tiredness?

Many people experience tiredness regularly. The key difference is how long it lasts, how severe it feels, and whether it improves with rest.

If fatigue feels unusual for you or continues without explanation, it is worth discussing with a doctor.

Other Symptoms That May Occur With Colon Cancer Fatigue

Fatigue alone is not enough to diagnose colon cancer. However, when combined with certain symptoms, it may require medical evaluation.

Possible colon cancer symptoms include:

Changes in Bowel Habits

Some people may notice:

  • Persistent constipation or diarrhoea
  • Changes in stool consistency
  • Feeling that the bowel does not empty completely

Blood in Stool

Blood in stool may appear as:

  • Bright red blood
  • Dark or black stools

Not all rectal bleeding is caused by cancer, but unexplained bleeding should always be checked.

Unexplained Weight Loss

Losing weight without changes in diet or exercise may indicate an underlying health issue that needs evaluation.

Abdominal Discomfort

Some people may experience:

  • Persistent abdominal pain
  • Cramping
  • Bloating
  • Changes in digestion

Weakness Due to Anaemia

Low iron levels caused by hidden bleeding may result in fatigue, weakness, and reduced stamina.

When Should You See a Doctor for Persistent Fatigue?

Occasional tiredness is common. However, medical advice may be needed when fatigue:

  • Lasts for several weeks without improvement
  • Affects daily activities
  • Occurs with unexplained weight loss
  • Is associated with changes in bowel habits
  • Occurs with blood in stool
  • Comes with symptoms of anaemia

A doctor may recommend tests based on your symptoms, medical history, and risk factors.

Common evaluations may include:

  • Blood tests to check haemoglobin and iron levels
  • Stool tests when appropriate
  • Colonoscopy to examine the colon
  • Imaging tests if required

Early evaluation can help identify the cause and guide appropriate treatment.

How Is Colon Cancer Fatigue Managed?

Managing fatigue involves addressing the underlying cause while supporting overall health.

Depending on individual needs, doctors may recommend:

Treating the Underlying Cancer

Appropriate cancer treatment can help reduce symptoms caused by tumour-related changes.

Managing Anaemia

If iron deficiency or anaemia is present, treatment may include:

  • Iron supplementation
  • Dietary guidance
  • Treating the source of blood loss

Maintaining Proper Nutrition

A balanced diet with adequate protein, vitamins, and minerals supports recovery and energy levels.

Gentle Physical Activity

Light activities such as walking, when medically suitable, may help improve strength and reduce fatigue.

Managing Sleep and Stress

Good sleep habits and emotional support can help patients cope better with ongoing fatigue.

If you are experiencing persistent digestive symptoms or unexplained fatigue, getting expert medical advice can help identify the cause early.

Yes, colon cancer can often be detected earlier through appropriate screening and timely medical evaluation.

Screening recommendations may depend on:

  • Age
  • Family history
  • Personal health risks
  • Previous bowel conditions

Early detection can improve treatment options and outcomes. People with warning symptoms should not ignore persistent changes in their health.

Frequently Asked Questions About Colon Cancer Fatigue

What does colon cancer fatigue feel like?

Colon cancer fatigue often feels like a persistent lack of energy that does not improve even after proper rest or sleep. People may feel unusually weak, tired during normal activities, or unable to maintain their usual routine.

Is fatigue an early symptom of colon cancer?

Fatigue can occur with colon cancer, but it is not always an early or specific symptom. It may happen due to factors such as hidden blood loss, iron deficiency anaemia, inflammation, or changes in the body caused by cancer. Persistent unexplained fatigue should be evaluated by a healthcare professional.

How is colon cancer fatigue different from normal tiredness?

Normal tiredness usually improves after rest, sleep, or recovery from physical activity. Colon cancer-related fatigue may continue despite adequate rest and may interfere with daily activities. It is often accompanied by other symptoms such as bowel changes, unexplained weight loss, or anaemia.

Can iron deficiency cause fatigue in colon cancer?

Yes. Colon cancer can sometimes cause slow bleeding in the digestive tract, which may lead to iron deficiency anaemia. Reduced iron levels can lower oxygen supply in the body and result in tiredness, weakness, and reduced energy.

What other symptoms can occur with colon cancer fatigue?

Other possible colon cancer symptoms may include changes in bowel habits, blood in stool, abdominal discomfort, unexplained weight loss, reduced appetite, and symptoms related to anaemia such as dizziness or weakness.

When should I see a doctor for constant tiredness?

You should consider consulting a doctor if fatigue lasts for several weeks, affects your daily life, occurs without a clear reason, or is accompanied by symptoms such as blood in stool, bowel changes, weight loss, or persistent abdominal discomfort.

Can colon cancer fatigue improve after treatment?

Yes, fatigue may improve when the underlying cause is treated. Managing cancer, correcting anaemia, improving nutrition, and following appropriate recovery strategies can help reduce fatigue levels.

What Is DG-HAL Laser Treatment for Piles?

DG-HAL (Doppler-Guided Hemorrhoidal Artery Ligation) is a minimally invasive procedure used to treat piles by identifying and reducing blood flow to the hemorrhoidal tissues.

During the procedure, a specialised Doppler device helps the doctor locate the arteries supplying blood to the piles. These blood vessels are then tied off, reducing blood flow and helping the enlarged hemorrhoidal tissue shrink gradually.

Unlike traditional piles surgery, DG-HAL focuses on treating the underlying blood supply rather than removing the hemorrhoidal tissue completely.

Some potential benefits of DG-HAL treatment include:

  • Minimally invasive approach
  • No major cutting or removal of hemorrhoidal tissue
  • Less discomfort compared to conventional surgical methods
  • Faster recovery for many patients
  • Suitable for selected cases of internal piles

However, the suitability of DG-HAL depends on the type and severity of piles.

How Many DG-HAL Laser Sittings Are Usually Required?

One of the most common questions patients ask is, “How many DG-HAL laser sittings are required for piles?”

In most cases, DG-HAL is completed in one treatment session. It is generally designed as a single-procedure treatment where the doctor addresses the affected hemorrhoidal arteries during the same sitting.

However, some patients may require additional evaluation or follow-up care depending on:

  • Grade of hemorrhoids
  • Number and size of hemorrhoidal cushions
  • Severity of symptoms
  • Presence of associated conditions like anal fissure or fistula
  • Response after treatment

The doctor may schedule follow-up visits to monitor healing and recovery, but these are usually not additional treatment sittings.

Factors That Decide the Number of DG-HAL Sessions Needed

Grade of Piles

The grade of piles plays an important role in deciding the treatment approach.

Grade 1 Piles

Grade 1 piles are usually small and remain inside the anal canal. They may often be managed with lifestyle changes, medicines, or minimally invasive treatments depending on symptoms.

Grade 2 Piles

Grade 2 piles may come out during bowel movements but return on their own. DG-HAL can be considered for suitable patients with symptomatic Grade 2 piles.

Grade 3 Piles

Grade 3 piles protrude during bowel movements and may require manual pushing back. Advanced treatments like DG-HAL may be recommended in selected cases.

Grade 4 Piles

Grade 4 piles remain permanently outside and may require different treatment approaches depending on the condition.

A detailed examination by a proctologist helps determine whether DG-HAL is appropriate.

Severity of Symptoms

Patients with mild symptoms may need less intervention compared to those experiencing:

  • Frequent bleeding
  • Persistent discomfort
  • Larger hemorrhoids
  • Repeated prolapse
  • Difficulty during bowel movements

A doctor evaluates symptoms along with clinical findings before recommending treatment.

Individual Healing Response

Every person’s recovery process is different. Factors such as diet, bowel habits, hydration, and following post-treatment instructions can influence healing.

Maintaining healthy bowel habits after DG-HAL can support recovery and reduce the chances of recurrence.

Is DG-HAL Laser Treatment a One-Time Procedure?

For many patients, DG-HAL is performed as a one-time procedure. The treatment is planned after a complete evaluation to address the affected hemorrhoidal arteries.

Patients usually do not need repeated laser sessions like some other treatments. However, follow-up appointments may be recommended to check recovery and ensure symptoms are improving.

The final treatment plan depends on the patient’s specific condition and should be decided after consultation with a qualified proctologist.

DG-HAL Treatment Process: What Patients Can Expect

Understanding the procedure can help reduce anxiety before treatment.

Consultation and Diagnosis

The doctor first evaluates symptoms, medical history, and the severity of piles. Additional examination may be performed if required.

Treatment Planning

Based on the findings, the doctor decides whether DG-HAL or another treatment option is suitable.

DG-HAL Procedure

During the procedure:

  • The doctor identifies hemorrhoidal arteries using Doppler guidance.
  • The blood vessels supplying the piles are ligated.
  • The reduced blood flow helps shrink the hemorrhoidal tissue.

The procedure duration may vary depending on the patient’s condition.

Recovery and Follow-Up

Most patients can gradually return to normal activities as advised by their doctor. Follow-up visits help monitor progress and recovery.

  • Piles that frequently come out during bowel movements

Early evaluation can help identify the right treatment option before symptoms become more severe.

DG-HAL Laser Treatment vs Traditional Piles Surgery

Patients often compare DG-HAL with conventional surgical methods before deciding on treatment. Both approaches have their own role, and the right choice depends on the patient’s condition.

DG-HAL Treatment

DG-HAL focuses on reducing blood flow to hemorrhoidal tissue using Doppler guidance.

Possible advantages include:

  • Minimally invasive procedure
  • Less tissue removal
  • Generally lower post-procedure discomfort
  • Faster return to routine activities for many patients

Traditional Hemorrhoid Surgery

Traditional surgery may involve removing hemorrhoidal tissue and may be recommended for certain advanced cases.

The treatment choice depends on factors such as:

  • Grade of piles
  • Size of hemorrhoids
  • Symptoms
  • Previous treatment history
  • Doctor’s clinical assessment

A consultation with an experienced proctologist helps determine the most suitable option.

Recovery After DG-HAL Treatment for Piles

Recovery after DG-HAL varies from person to person. Many patients experience gradual improvement in symptoms after treatment.

During recovery, doctors may recommend:

  • Maintaining adequate water intake
  • Eating a fibre-rich diet
  • Avoiding straining during bowel movements
  • Following prescribed medications
  • Keeping the anal area clean
  • Attending follow-up appointments

Healthy bowel habits play an important role in preventing future problems.

How Long Does It Take to See Results After DG-HAL?

The improvement timeline after DG-HAL can vary depending on the severity of piles and individual healing response.

Some patients may notice symptom improvement within a short period, while others may experience gradual changes over several weeks.

The treated hemorrhoidal tissue reduces in size as the blood supply decreases. Regular follow-up helps the doctor assess progress.

Does DG-HAL Laser Treatment Prevent Piles From Coming Back?

DG-HAL can help treat piles by addressing the blood supply contributing to hemorrhoidal enlargement. However, maintaining healthy lifestyle habits is important to reduce the risk of recurrence.

Factors that may help prevent piles problems include:

  • Eating enough fibre

Recovery time varies between individuals. Many patients can gradually return to daily activities based on their doctor’s advice.

While DG-HAL can effectively treat piles in suitable cases, maintaining healthy bowel habits, avoiding constipation, and following medical advice can help reduce the chances of recurrence.

What Is PREFACT for Anal Fistula?

PREFACT (Primary Fistula Repair with Advancement of Closure Technique) is a minimally invasive approach used for treating anal fistulas. The procedure focuses on closing the internal opening of the fistula tract while reducing injury to the surrounding anal muscles.

An anal fistula is an abnormal tunnel that develops between the inside of the anal canal and the skin near the anus. It commonly develops after an infection or abscess in the anal glands.

Traditional fistula surgeries may involve cutting part of the fistula tract, which can sometimes affect surrounding tissues. Advanced techniques like PREFACT aim to treat the fistula while preserving normal anatomy.

The suitability of PREFACT depends on factors such as:

  • Type of fistula
  • Location of the fistula tract
  • Complexity of the condition
  • Previous fistula treatments
  • Patient’s overall health

Understanding Anal Fistula Before PREFACT Treatment

What Happens in an Anal Fistula?

An anal fistula usually develops when an infected anal gland forms an abscess. If the abscess does not heal completely, a small tunnel can remain between the anal canal and the skin.

Common symptoms of anal fistula include:

  • Repeated discharge or pus near the anus
  • Pain or swelling around the anal region
  • Skin irritation or itching
  • Recurrent abscess formation
  • Discomfort while sitting
  • Foul-smelling discharge

Ignoring symptoms may allow the fistula tract to persist or become more complicated over time.

Why Does Anal Fistula Require Treatment?

Unlike some conditions that heal naturally, anal fistulas usually do not close on their own because the abnormal tract continues to receive fluid or infection from inside the anal canal.

Without proper treatment, a fistula may lead to:

  • Recurring infections
  • Repeated pain and swelling
  • Abscess formation
  • Continuous discharge
  • Impact on daily comfort and confidence

Early evaluation by a qualified proctologist can help identify the right treatment approach.

How Is the PREFACT Procedure Performed?

The PREFACT procedure involves careful evaluation and closure of the fistula opening while aiming to protect the anal sphincter muscles.

Step 1: Patient Evaluation

Before the procedure, the doctor examines the fistula and may recommend imaging tests such as MRI fistulography to understand:

  • The path of the fistula tract
  • Internal and external openings
  • Complexity of the fistula

This helps the surgeon plan the most suitable treatment strategy.

Step 2: Identification of the Fistula Tract

During the procedure, the surgeon identifies the fistula pathway and prepares the tract for treatment.

The main focus is to address the source of the fistula while preserving surrounding healthy tissues.

Step 3: Closure of the Internal Opening

The internal opening, which connects the fistula to the anal canal, plays an important role in fistula formation.

PREFACT focuses on closing this opening to reduce the chance of continued infection and discharge.

Step 4: Recovery and Follow-Up

After the procedure, patients receive instructions regarding:

  • Wound care
  • Diet and bowel habits
  • Medication use
  • Follow-up visits

Regular follow-up helps doctors monitor healing and recovery.

What Are the Benefits of PREFACT for Anal Fistula?

PREFACT is designed as a tissue-preserving approach for suitable anal fistula cases. The potential benefits include:

1. Focus on Preserving Anal Sphincter Muscles

The anal sphincter muscles control bowel movements. Protecting these muscles is an important consideration during fistula treatment.

PREFACT aims to minimize unnecessary damage to surrounding muscles.

2. Minimally Invasive Treatment Approach

Compared with some traditional surgical methods, minimally invasive fistula procedures may involve less tissue disruption.

This can support a smoother recovery experience for eligible patients.

3. Reduced Post-Procedure Discomfort

Because the technique focuses on preserving healthy tissues, some patients may experience reduced discomfort compared with more extensive procedures.

However, recovery experiences can vary depending on individual conditions.

4. Faster Return to Daily Activities

Many minimally invasive approaches are designed to help patients resume normal activities sooner after treatment.

The exact recovery timeline depends on:

  • Fistula complexity
  • Healing response
  • Procedure performed
  • Doctor’s recommendations

5. Suitable for Selected Complex Cases

Some fistulas are more challenging because of their location or involvement with anal muscles.

Advanced techniques like PREFACT may be considered when conventional approaches require careful planning.

Traditional procedures and newer minimally invasive techniques have different approaches.

Who May Not Be Suitable for PREFACT?

PREFACT may not be recommended in some situations, including:

What Are External Piles?

External piles are swollen veins that develop under the skin around the anus. Unlike internal piles, which occur inside the rectum, external piles form outside the anal opening and can be more noticeable.

They may appear as small lumps or swelling and can cause symptoms such as:

  • Pain while sitting or walking
  • Itching and irritation around the anus
  • Swelling near the anal opening
  • Bleeding during bowel movements
  • A painful lump due to blood clot formation (thrombosed external piles)

External piles can sometimes settle with conservative treatment. However, when symptoms continue or affect daily activities, surgical removal may be considered.

When Is Surgery Recommended for External Piles?

Not every case of external piles requires surgery. Doctors usually recommend surgical treatment when symptoms are severe, recurring, or do not improve with other treatments.

Harmonic excision may be considered for patients with:

Persistent Pain and Discomfort

Large external piles can create continuous discomfort, especially during sitting, walking, or bowel movements.

Repeated Episodes of Swelling

Some patients experience repeated flare-ups where piles become swollen and painful despite medications and lifestyle changes.

Thrombosed External Piles

A blood clot inside an external pile can cause sudden and intense pain. In some cases, removal of the affected tissue may provide relief.

Failure of Non-Surgical Treatments

If dietary changes, medications, and other conservative methods do not provide relief, surgery may be advised.

What Is Harmonic Excision of External Piles?

Harmonic excision is a surgical technique that uses a specialised device called a harmonic scalpel. The instrument uses ultrasonic vibrations to cut and seal blood vessels at the same time.

Unlike traditional cutting methods, this technology allows surgeons to work with controlled energy and improved precision.

The main goal of the procedure is to:

  • Remove problematic piles tissue
  • Minimise bleeding during surgery
  • Reduce surrounding tissue injury
  • Support faster recovery

The suitability of harmonic excision depends on the patient’s condition, pile size, symptoms, and surgeon evaluation.

How Does Harmonic Excision of External Piles Work?

The procedure is usually performed under anaesthesia to ensure patient comfort.

Step 1: Pre-Surgery Evaluation

Before surgery, the doctor examines the piles and may review:

  • Symptoms and duration
  • Previous treatments
  • Medical history
  • Any associated conditions

The doctor explains the procedure, preparation instructions, and expected recovery process.

Step 2: Anaesthesia Administration

Anaesthesia is given based on the patient’s requirement and surgical plan. This helps prevent pain during the procedure.

Step 3: Removal of External Piles

The surgeon carefully identifies the affected piles tissue and removes it using the harmonic device.

The ultrasonic energy helps cut tissue while sealing small blood vessels, which may help reduce bleeding during the procedure.

Step 4: Completion of Procedure

After removing the piles, the surgical area is managed according to the treatment plan. Patients are monitored for a period before discharge.

Benefits of Harmonic Excision for External Piles

Harmonic excision offers several potential advantages compared with some conventional surgical approaches.

Better Surgical Precision

The harmonic device allows surgeons to target the affected tissue while controlling surrounding tissue impact.

Reduced Bleeding During Surgery

Since the device seals blood vessels while cutting, it may help minimise bleeding during the procedure.

Less Tissue Trauma

Controlled energy delivery can help reduce unnecessary tissue damage.

Comfortable Recovery

Many patients experience a smoother recovery process with appropriate post-operative care and follow-up.

Shorter Procedure Time

The technique can allow efficient removal of piles tissue, depending on the complexity of the case.

Patients often want to understand how harmonic excision differs from conventional hemorrhoid surgery.

The right procedure depends on factors such as piles severity, symptoms, medical history, and surgeon recommendation.

Keeping the Area Clean

Following Activity Guidelines

Why Is Treating Anal Fistula Important?

What Is Anal Fistula Glue Plug Treatment?

Anal fistula glue plug treatment is a minimally invasive procedure designed to close the fistula tract using a specially developed medical material.

Unlike traditional fistula surgery methods that may involve cutting open the tract, the glue plug technique focuses on sealing the internal pathway and supporting natural healing.

The procedure involves placing a biocompatible plug or adhesive material into the fistula tract. Over time, the body’s healing process helps form new tissue around the treated area, gradually closing the abnormal tunnel.

This approach may help reduce damage to surrounding tissues and preserve anal sphincter function.

How Does Fistula Glue Plug Treatment Work?

The procedure generally involves the following steps:

1. Diagnosis and Fistula Mapping

This helps identify:

  • The internal opening of the fistula
  • The external opening on the skin
  • Length and pathway of the tract
  • Complexity of the fistula

Accurate mapping helps doctors select the most appropriate treatment method.

2. Cleaning the Fistula Tract

During the procedure, the fistula tract is cleaned to remove infected tissue and debris. This prepares the area for placement of the plug or glue material.

Proper cleaning is important because infection inside the tract can affect healing.

3. Placement of the Glue Plug

The medical plug or adhesive material is carefully placed inside the fistula tract. The material acts as a framework that supports tissue growth and closure.

The goal is to close the abnormal connection while avoiding unnecessary injury to the anal muscles.

4. Healing and Follow-Up

After the procedure, new tissue gradually develops around the treated area. Regular follow-up appointments help doctors monitor healing progress.

Patients are usually advised about:

What Is Fistula and Why Does It Need Treatment?

An anal fistula is an abnormal tunnel that develops between the inside of the anal canal and the surrounding skin. It often develops after an infection or abscess near the anal glands.

When untreated, a fistula may continue to cause symptoms such as:

  • Persistent discharge near the anal opening
  • Pain or discomfort while sitting
  • Swelling or irritation around the affected area
  • Repeated formation of abscesses
  • Unpleasant odour due to discharge

Unlike some minor conditions that resolve on their own, fistulas usually require medical evaluation because the tract may continue to remain active.

Early diagnosis helps determine the type, complexity, and most suitable treatment approach.

What Is Kshara Sutra for Fistula?

Kshara Sutra is an Ayurvedic thread therapy used in the management of fistula-in-ano. The word “Kshara” refers to alkaline herbal substances, while “Sutra” means thread.

During this procedure, a specially prepared medicated thread is placed through the fistulous tract. The thread contains herbal alkaline preparations that help in gradual cleansing of the tract and support the natural healing process.

The therapy works through a controlled process where the thread is periodically changed, allowing the fistula tract to gradually reduce and heal.

How Does Kshara Sutra Therapy Work?

Kshara Sutra therapy works through multiple actions:

1. Cleansing of the Fistulous Tract

The medicinal coating on the thread helps remove unhealthy tissue and supports cleaning of the fistula pathway.

2. Gradual Cutting and Healing Process

The thread gradually works through the tract while allowing healing to occur simultaneously. This controlled process is known as “cutting and healing” action.

3. Prevention of Recurrence

By addressing the fistulous pathway rather than only managing symptoms, Kshara Sutra aims to support complete healing of the tract.

The exact treatment duration depends on factors such as:

  • Length and depth of the fistula tract
  • Type of fistula
  • Presence of infection
  • Individual healing response

What Is Kshara Karma for Fistula?

Kshara Karma is another Ayurvedic procedure that uses Kshara (alkaline herbal preparations) for therapeutic purposes.

In fistula management, Kshara Karma may be considered in selected cases where controlled application of herbal alkaline substances can support tissue management and healing.

A qualified Ayurvedic proctology specialist evaluates the condition before recommending the appropriate procedure.

Difference Between Kshara Sutra and Kshara Karma

Diagnosis and Assessment

The doctor first evaluates:

  • Fistula location
  • Number of openings
  • Depth and direction of the tract
  • Previous treatment history

Imaging or examination techniques may be recommended in complex cases.

Placement of the Medicated Thread

The Kshara Sutra thread is carefully placed through the fistulous pathway under medical supervision.

Regular Thread Changes

The thread is changed at scheduled intervals. This helps maintain the therapeutic effect while allowing gradual healing.

Follow-Up and Recovery Monitoring

Regular follow-ups help doctors monitor healing progress and manage any discomfort during treatment.

The sharp pain, burning sensation, and occasional bleeding associated with fissures can significantly affect daily comfort and quality of life. While many anal fissures improve with medications, dietary changes, and lifestyle modifications, some become chronic and may require surgical treatment.

Sphincterotomy for anal fissure is a commonly performed surgical procedure recommended for chronic fissures that do not heal with conservative treatments. The procedure works by relaxing the tight internal anal sphincter muscle, improving blood flow to the affected area, and allowing the fissure to heal.

At Chirag Global Hospitals, Bangalore, specialists evaluate each patient’s symptoms, medical history, and condition before suggesting the most suitable treatment approach. Understanding the procedure, possible risks, and recovery process can help patients make informed decisions about their health.

What Is Sphincterotomy for Anal Fissure?

Sphincterotomy is a surgical procedure used to treat chronic anal fissures by reducing pressure caused by the internal anal sphincter muscle.

An anal fissure is a small tear in the delicate lining of the anal canal. When this tear occurs, the internal sphincter muscle may tighten or go into spasm. This increased pressure can reduce blood circulation to the area, making healing difficult.

During a lateral internal sphincterotomy procedure, the surgeon carefully cuts a small portion of the internal sphincter muscle. This helps relax the muscle, decreases pressure, improves blood supply, and supports natural healing.

The procedure is generally considered when:

  • The fissure has not healed after several weeks of treatment.
  • Pain continues despite medicines and lifestyle changes.
  • Symptoms frequently return.
  • Muscle spasms are preventing healing.
  • Chronic fissure symptoms affect daily activities.

Acute vs Chronic Anal Fissure: When Surgery May Be Needed

Not all fissures require surgery. Understanding the difference between acute and chronic fissures helps determine the appropriate treatment approach.

Acute Anal Fissure

An acute fissure is a recent tear that usually develops due to:

  • Passing hard stools.
  • Constipation.
  • Straining during bowel movements.
  • Diarrhoea or frequent bowel irritation.

Many acute fissures improve with:

  • Increased fibre intake.
  • Adequate hydration.
  • Stool softeners.
  • Warm sitz baths.
  • Doctor-prescribed medicines.

Chronic Anal Fissure

A fissure is considered chronic when it persists for a longer duration or repeatedly returns.

Common features include:

  • Persistent anal pain.
  • A visible tear or ulcer-like area.
  • Sentinel skin tag near the fissure.
  • Tight internal sphincter muscle.
  • Repeated bleeding during bowel movements.

For chronic fissures that do not respond to medical treatment, anal fissure surgery such as sphincterotomy may be recommended.

How Is the Sphincterotomy Procedure Performed?

A sphincterotomy is usually performed as a minimally invasive procedure. The exact technique may vary depending on the patient’s condition and the surgeon’s assessment.

Step 1: Consultation and Evaluation

Before surgery, the doctor evaluates:

  • Duration of fissure symptoms.
  • Severity of pain.
  • Previous treatments tried.
  • Bowel habits.
  • Overall health condition.

A physical examination helps confirm whether the symptoms are caused by an anal fissure and whether surgery is suitable.

Step 2: Anaesthesia

The procedure is performed under anaesthesia to ensure patient comfort. The type of anaesthesia depends on the patient’s health status and surgical requirements.

Options may include:

  • Local anaesthesia.
  • Regional anaesthesia.
  • General anaesthesia.

Step 3: Internal Sphincter Muscle Relaxation

During lateral internal sphincterotomy:

  • A small incision is made near the anal canal.
  • A controlled portion of the internal sphincter muscle is divided.
  • Muscle tension is reduced.
  • Blood circulation improves around the fissure.
  • Healing can occur more effectively.

The procedure is usually completed within a short duration, and many patients may be discharged after monitoring.

Who Is a Suitable Candidate for Sphincterotomy?

Sphincterotomy may be considered for patients who:

  • Have chronic anal fissures.
  • Experience recurring fissure symptoms.
  • Have not improved with medicines or lifestyle changes.
  • Have severe sphincter muscle tightness.
  • Continue to experience pain and bleeding.

However, the final decision depends on a specialist’s evaluation. Some patients may benefit from alternative treatments depending on their symptoms and medical history.

Benefits of Sphincterotomy for Anal Fissure

For appropriate candidates, sphincterotomy can help address the main factor responsible for delayed fissure healing — excessive sphincter pressure.

Potential Benefits Include:

  • Reduction in anal muscle spasm.
  • Improved blood flow to the affected area.
  • Relief from chronic fissure pain.
  • Lower chances of repeated fissure episodes.
  • Faster healing compared with continued conservative management in selected cases.

The outcome of surgery depends on individual factors such as overall health, severity of fissure, and post-operative care.

Recovery After Sphincterotomy Surgery

Understanding the recovery process can help patients prepare better after surgery.

Most patients gradually experience improvement as the sphincter muscle relaxes and the fissure begins to heal.

Immediately After Surgery

Patients may notice:

  • Mild discomfort around the surgical area.
  • Minor bleeding or discharge.
  • Temporary changes during bowel movements.

Doctors may advise:

  • Pain medications if required.
  • Fibre-rich foods.
  • Increased fluid intake.
  • Stool softeners.
  • Warm sitz baths.

First Few Weeks After Surgery

During recovery, patients should:

  • Avoid constipation.
  • Prevent excessive straining.
  • Maintain proper hygiene.
  • Follow prescribed medications.
  • Attend follow-up consultations.

A balanced diet and healthy bowel habits play an important role in preventing recurrence.

How to Support Faster Healing After Anal Fissure Surgery

Follow a Fibre-Rich Diet

A high-fibre diet helps create softer stools and reduces pressure during bowel movements.

Good fibre sources include:

  • Fruits.
  • Vegetables.
  • Whole grains.
  • Pulses.
  • Fibre supplements recommended by doctors.

Drink Enough Water

Proper hydration supports healthy digestion and helps prevent constipation.

Avoid Straining During Bowel Movements

Repeated straining can irritate the healing area and may slow recovery.

Maintain Good Anal Hygiene

Keeping the area clean and following post-operative instructions can support comfortable healing.

Risks and Possible Complications of Sphincterotomy

Like any surgical procedure, sphincterotomy for anal fissure has certain risks. Although many patients recover well, understanding possible complications helps set realistic expectations before surgery.

The likelihood of complications depends on factors such as overall health, previous treatments, surgical technique, and post-operative care.

Possible Risks Include:

Temporary Pain or Discomfort

Some patients may experience mild pain, soreness, or discomfort after surgery. This usually improves as healing progresses and can often be managed with prescribed medications.

Bleeding

Minor bleeding after sphincterotomy may occur during the initial recovery period. However, heavy or persistent bleeding should be reported to the doctor.

Infection

As with any surgical procedure, there is a small risk of infection. Following wound care instructions and maintaining hygiene can help reduce this risk.

Difficulty Controlling Gas or Stool

The internal anal sphincter plays a role in bowel control. In some cases, patients may experience temporary difficulty controlling gas or minor leakage after surgery.

Most patients do not experience significant long-term problems, but discussing individual risks with a qualified surgeon is important before undergoing the procedure.

Recurrence of Anal Fissure

Although sphincterotomy helps many patients with chronic fissures, recurrence is possible, especially if factors such as constipation, hard stools, or unhealthy bowel habits continue.

Sphincterotomy vs Other Anal Fissure Treatments

Treatment for anal fissure depends on whether the condition is acute or chronic and how the patient responds to initial therapies.

Medical Treatment

For many early-stage fissures, doctors may recommend non-surgical approaches such as:

  • Fibre supplements.
  • Stool softeners.
  • Warm sitz baths.
  • Topical medications.
  • Lifestyle changes.

These methods aim to reduce constipation, relax muscle tension, and support healing.

Botox Injection for Anal Fissure

Botulinum toxin injections may be used to temporarily relax the internal anal sphincter muscle.

Potential benefits:

  • Minimally invasive.
  • Does not involve cutting the muscle.
  • May be suitable for selected patients.

However, the effects may be temporary, and some patients may require additional treatment.

Sphincterotomy Surgery

Sphincterotomy directly reduces internal sphincter pressure by making a controlled surgical cut.

It may be considered when:

  • Medical treatments have not worked.
  • Symptoms continue for a long time.
  • The fissure repeatedly returns.

A proctology specialist can help determine which option is appropriate based on individual symptoms.

How Long Does Recovery Take After Sphincterotomy?

Recovery time after anal fissure surgery varies from person to person.

Many patients can return to normal activities gradually after a short recovery period, depending on their comfort level and doctor’s advice.

General Recovery Timeline

First Few Days:

  • Mild discomfort may occur.
  • Bowel movements may feel different.
  • Pain management and stool regulation are important.

First Few Weeks:

  • Surgical area continues healing.
  • Bowel movements usually become more comfortable.
  • Patients should maintain fibre intake and hydration.

Following Weeks:

  • Symptoms generally continue improving.
  • Follow-up appointments help monitor recovery.

The complete healing process depends on the severity of the fissure and individual healing response.

When Should You Consult a Doctor for Anal Fissure?

Many people delay treatment because they assume anal pain will resolve on its own. However, persistent symptoms should be evaluated by a healthcare professional.

Consult a doctor if you experience:

  • Sharp pain during bowel movements.
  • Bleeding from the anus.
  • Symptoms lasting more than several weeks.
  • Repeated fissures.
  • Pain affecting daily activities.
  • A lump or skin tag near the anal opening.

Early diagnosis can help prevent the condition from becoming chronic.

What is sphincterotomy for anal fissure?

Sphincterotomy is a surgical procedure used to treat chronic anal fissures by relaxing part of the internal anal sphincter muscle. This reduces muscle pressure, improves blood flow, and supports fissure healing.

How long does sphincterotomy surgery take?

The procedure is usually completed within a short duration. The exact time depends on the patient’s condition and the surgical approach used.

Is sphincterotomy painful?

The procedure is performed under anaesthesia, so patients generally do not feel pain during surgery. Mild discomfort may occur during recovery and can usually be managed with medications and proper care.

How long does it take to recover after anal fissure surgery?

Recovery varies between individuals. Many patients gradually return to normal activities within a short period, while complete healing depends on the fissure condition and post-operative care.

What are the risks of sphincterotomy surgery?

Possible risks include bleeding, infection, temporary changes in bowel control, discomfort, and recurrence of fissure symptoms. Your surgeon can explain risks based on your specific health condition.

Can anal fissure heal without surgery?

Yes, many acute fissures improve with dietary changes, medications, hydration, and proper bowel habits. Surgery is usually considered for chronic fissures that do not respond to other treatments.

Is sphincterotomy a permanent treatment for anal fissure?

Sphincterotomy can provide long-term relief for many patients with chronic fissures. However, maintaining healthy bowel habits is important to reduce the chance of recurrence.

What Is Proctoscopy?

Proctoscopy is a diagnostic examination that uses a specialised instrument called a proctoscope to view the lining of the anal canal and lower part of the rectum.

The procedure allows doctors to directly examine areas that cannot be assessed through a regular physical examination. It is commonly performed when patients have symptoms related to the lower digestive tract.

A proctoscope is a short, hollow tube with a light source that helps doctors get a clear view of the internal structures. The examination is usually quick and may be performed in an outpatient setting.

Why Is Proctoscopy Done for Rectal Problems?

Doctors recommend proctoscopy when symptoms suggest problems affecting the anus or rectum. The test helps identify the possible cause of symptoms and supports accurate diagnosis.

Common reasons for undergoing a proctoscopy examination include:

Evaluation of Rectal Bleeding

Blood during bowel movements is one of the common reasons patients seek medical attention. While piles are a frequent cause, rectal bleeding can occur due to different conditions.

Proctoscopy can help doctors examine the lower rectum and identify possible sources of bleeding.

Diagnosis of Haemorrhoids (Piles)

Internal piles develop inside the rectum and may not always be visible externally. Proctoscopy allows doctors to examine internal haemorrhoids and assess their severity.

The findings can help determine whether conservative treatment, medication, lifestyle changes, or procedures may be required.

Assessment of Anal Pain and Discomfort

Persistent anal pain may occur due to conditions such as:

  • Anal fissures
  • Inflammation
  • Infection
  • Rectal abnormalities

A detailed examination helps identify the cause and plan appropriate management.

Detection of Abnormal Growths or Polyps

In some cases, proctoscopy may reveal abnormal tissue growths or polyps in the lower rectum. Doctors may recommend further evaluation depending on the findings.

Monitoring Existing Rectal Conditions

Patients undergoing treatment for certain rectal disorders may require follow-up examinations to monitor improvement or changes.

What Conditions Can Proctoscopy Detect?

A proctoscopy examination can help evaluate several anal and rectal conditions, including:

1. Internal Haemorrhoids

Internal piles are swollen blood vessels inside the rectum. They may cause:

  • Bright red bleeding during stools
  • A feeling of incomplete bowel evacuation
  • Mucus discharge
  • Prolapse in advanced cases

Proctoscopy helps doctors view the internal haemorrhoidal tissue and determine the extent of the condition.

2. Anal Fissures

An anal fissure is a small tear in the lining of the anal canal. It commonly causes sharp pain during or after passing stools.

Although many fissures are diagnosed through physical examination, proctoscopy may be used in selected cases to assess associated changes.

3. Rectal Inflammation

Inflammation in the rectum, known as proctitis, may occur due to infections, inflammatory bowel conditions, or other causes.

Proctoscopy helps doctors examine signs of inflammation and decide further investigations if required.

4. Rectal Polyps and Other Abnormalities

Abnormal tissue changes inside the rectum may require detailed assessment. If unusual findings are observed, doctors may suggest additional tests or biopsy procedures.

How Is a Proctoscopy Procedure Performed?

Many patients feel anxious before a rectal examination because they do not know what to expect. Understanding the procedure can make the experience more comfortable.

The typical steps include:

Before the Procedure

The doctor may discuss:

  • Your symptoms
  • Medical history
  • Previous treatments
  • Bowel-related concerns

In some cases, bowel preparation or an enema may be recommended to clear the rectum before examination.

During the Examination

During the procedure:

  1. The patient is positioned comfortably as advised by the doctor.
  2. A lubricated proctoscope is gently inserted into the anal canal.
  3. The doctor examines the rectal lining using the light attached to the instrument.
  4. The procedure usually takes only a few minutes.

Patients may feel mild pressure or the sensation of needing to pass stool, but severe pain is not expected in most cases.

After the Procedure

Most people can return to normal activities soon after the examination. The doctor will explain the findings and discuss whether further tests or treatment are needed.

Is Proctoscopy Painful?

A common concern among patients is whether a proctoscopy examination is painful.

Generally, proctoscopy is considered a quick and well-tolerated procedure. Some people may experience:

  • Mild discomfort
  • Pressure sensation
  • Temporary urge to pass stool

If a patient has severe inflammation, an active fissure, or significant pain, the doctor may take additional precautions to ensure comfort.

Discussing concerns openly with your doctor can help make the examination easier and less stressful.

Although both procedures examine parts of the digestive tract, they are performed for different purposes.

The doctor decides which examination is appropriate based on symptoms, age, medical history, and clinical findings.

Patients experiencing ongoing rectal symptoms should not ignore them. A timely evaluation can help identify the cause and prevent complications.

This helps ensure a safer examination.

Maintain Relaxation During the Procedure

Feeling nervous before a rectal examination is common. Understanding the process and communicating concerns with your healthcare provider can make the experience more comfortable.

Accurate Diagnosis

The procedure provides a direct view of the anal canal and lower rectum, helping doctors identify abnormalities more accurately.

Myth 3: Rectal Problems Will Resolve Without Medical Attention

What Is Pelvic Floor Dysfunction?

The pelvic floor is a group of muscles, tissues, and ligaments located at the bottom of the pelvis. These muscles support important organs, including the bladder, rectum, and reproductive organs.

During a normal bowel movement, the pelvic floor muscles should relax while the abdominal muscles contract to help move stool through the rectum. When this coordination is disrupted, it can result in difficulty emptying the bowel.

Pelvic floor dysfunction occurs when these muscles become too tight, weak, or poorly coordinated, affecting normal bowel, bladder, and pelvic functions.

How Does Pelvic Floor Dysfunction Cause Constipation?

Many people assume constipation only happens because of slow digestion. However, problems with the muscles involved in bowel evacuation can also contribute significantly.

In people with pelvic floor dysfunction, the muscles around the rectum may not relax properly when trying to pass stool. Instead of opening smoothly, the muscles may tighten, creating resistance.

This condition is sometimes known as dyssynergic defecation, where the muscles involved in bowel movement work against each other rather than together.

Common ways pelvic floor dysfunction affects bowel movements include:

  • Difficulty starting a bowel movement
  • Excessive straining while passing stool
  • Feeling that stool has not completely emptied
  • Spending a long time in the bathroom
  • Hard or fragmented stools
  • Frequent urge to pass stool without complete relief
  • Dependence on laxatives for bowel movements

Common Symptoms of Pelvic Floor Dysfunction Related to Constipation

Recognising the symptoms early can help in getting appropriate evaluation and treatment.

1. Persistent Constipation

People with pelvic floor dysfunction often experience long-term constipation that does not improve significantly with dietary changes or increased fibre intake.

2. Straining During Bowel Movements

Repeated pushing or excessive effort during bowel movements may indicate that the pelvic muscles are not relaxing properly.

3. Feeling of Incomplete Evacuation

A common symptom is the sensation that stool remains inside the rectum even after using the toilet.

4. Difficulty Passing Stool Despite the Urge

Some individuals feel the need to pass stool but are unable to empty their bowel comfortably.

5. Pelvic or Rectal Discomfort

Muscle tension and poor coordination may contribute to discomfort, pressure, or pain around the pelvic and rectal area.

What Causes Pelvic Floor Dysfunction?

Pelvic floor dysfunction can develop due to several factors affecting muscle strength, coordination, and nerve function.

Common causes include:

Chronic Straining

Repeatedly straining during bowel movements can affect pelvic floor muscle coordination over time.

Long-Term Constipation

Chronic constipation can create a cycle where difficulty passing stool further affects normal bowel habits.

Pregnancy and Childbirth

Pregnancy-related changes and childbirth can impact pelvic floor muscles, leading to weakness or coordination issues.

Age-Related Muscle Changes

As people age, muscle strength and nerve coordination may change, affecting bowel control.

Previous Pelvic Surgery or Injury

Certain surgeries or injuries involving the pelvic region may influence muscle function.

Stress and Muscle Tension

Stress can contribute to increased muscle tightness, which may affect relaxation during bowel movements.

Difference Between Regular Constipation and Pelvic Floor Dysfunction

Not all constipation is caused by pelvic floor problems. Understanding the difference can help determine when specialist evaluation may be needed.

People with ongoing symptoms despite following healthy habits should consider a detailed evaluation.

How Is Pelvic Floor Dysfunction Diagnosed?

A proper diagnosis helps determine whether constipation is caused by pelvic muscle problems or other digestive conditions.

A specialist may recommend:

Medical History Evaluation

Doctors review symptoms, bowel habits, diet, previous treatments, and duration of constipation.

Physical Examination

A clinical examination may help assess pelvic muscle strength and coordination.

Anorectal Manometry

This test measures pressure and muscle coordination in the rectum and anal canal during bowel movements.

Defecography

This imaging test evaluates how the pelvic muscles function during stool evacuation.

Other Investigations

Depending on symptoms, doctors may suggest additional tests to rule out other causes of constipation.

Treatment Options for Pelvic Floor Dysfunction and Constipation

Treatment depends on the severity of symptoms and the underlying cause.

Pelvic Floor Rehabilitation

Pelvic floor therapy focuses on improving muscle coordination. It may include exercises and techniques that teach the muscles to relax and function correctly.

Biofeedback Therapy

Biofeedback helps patients understand how their pelvic muscles work and learn better control during bowel movements.

Dietary and Lifestyle Changes

Doctors may recommend:

  • Increasing fibre intake gradually
  • Drinking adequate fluids
  • Maintaining regular toilet habits
  • Staying physically active
  • Avoiding excessive straining

Medication Support

In some cases, medications may be recommended to soften stools or improve bowel movement frequency. These should be used under medical guidance.

Surgical Evaluation When Required

If constipation is caused by structural problems or other colorectal conditions, additional treatment approaches may be considered.

  • A constant feeling of incomplete bowel evacuation
  • Dependence on laxatives for regular bowel movements
  • Changes in bowel habits without an obvious reason

A detailed evaluation can help identify whether the problem is related to pelvic floor dysfunction, digestive disorders, lifestyle factors, or another underlying condition.

Lifestyle Tips to Support Healthy Bowel Function

While medical evaluation is important for persistent constipation, healthy daily habits can support better bowel function.

Maintain Adequate Fibre Intake

Fibre helps add bulk to stools and supports smoother bowel movements. Include fibre-rich foods such as:

  • Fruits
  • Vegetables
  • Whole grains
  • Legumes
  • Nuts and seeds

Increase fibre gradually to avoid bloating or discomfort.

Stay Hydrated

Adequate fluid intake helps maintain softer stools and supports normal digestion.

Avoid Excessive Straining

Repeated forceful straining can place pressure on pelvic floor muscles and may worsen bowel movement difficulties.

Develop Healthy Toilet Habits

Try to:

  • Respond to the urge to pass stool
  • Avoid delaying bowel movements frequently
  • Maintain a relaxed posture while using the toilet

Stay Physically Active

Regular movement can support intestinal activity and overall digestive health.

Can Pelvic Floor Exercises Help Constipation?

Pelvic floor exercises can be helpful when they are performed correctly and are recommended based on the individual’s condition.

Many people associate pelvic floor exercises only with strengthening muscles. However, constipation related to pelvic floor dysfunction often involves poor muscle relaxation and coordination rather than simple weakness.

A trained healthcare professional may recommend specific exercises or pelvic floor therapy techniques that focus on:

  • Improving muscle awareness
  • Learning proper relaxation
  • Coordinating abdominal and pelvic muscles
  • Improving bowel evacuation patterns

Performing incorrect exercises without understanding the underlying problem may not provide the expected benefit.

Pelvic Floor Dysfunction and Constipation in Bangalore: Getting the Right Care

Chronic constipation can have multiple causes, and identifying the exact reason is important for effective management. Symptoms caused by pelvic floor dysfunction require a different approach compared to constipation caused by diet, medication, or slow bowel movement.

FAQs

What is pelvic floor dysfunction and how does it cause constipation?

Pelvic floor dysfunction occurs when the muscles involved in bowel control do not relax or coordinate properly during stool passage. This can make it difficult to empty the bowel and may lead to chronic constipation, straining, and incomplete evacuation.

Can pelvic floor dysfunction be a reason for chronic constipation?

Yes. Pelvic floor dysfunction can contribute to chronic constipation, especially when a person has difficulty passing stool despite making dietary changes, increasing fibre intake, or using standard constipation treatments.

What are the symptoms of pelvic floor dysfunction-related constipation?

Common symptoms include difficulty passing stool, excessive straining, incomplete bowel emptying, prolonged toilet time, rectal discomfort, and repeated constipation episodes.

How is pelvic floor dysfunction diagnosed?

Doctors may use symptom evaluation, physical examination, anorectal manometry, defecography, and other tests to understand pelvic muscle coordination and identify the cause of constipation.

Can pelvic floor therapy treat constipation?

Pelvic floor therapy can help some people with constipation caused by muscle coordination problems. Techniques such as biofeedback therapy may help patients learn better muscle control during bowel movements.

Is pelvic floor dysfunction common in adults?

Pelvic floor dysfunction can affect adults of different ages. It may occur due to factors such as chronic straining, childbirth, ageing, pelvic injuries, or long-term bowel problems.

When should I see a constipation specialist in Bangalore?

You should consult a specialist if constipation continues for a long time, affects daily activities, requires frequent laxative use, or is associated with symptoms such as bleeding, pain, or unexplained weight changes.

Persistent constipation and repeated straining during bowel movements may seem like common digestive issues, but over time they can put excessive pressure on the muscles and tissues supporting the rectum. This continuous strain may contribute to conditions such as rectal prolapse, where part of the rectum slips out through the anal opening.

Understanding the connection between chronic straining and rectal prolapse is important because early evaluation and appropriate care can help prevent symptoms from worsening. What Is Rectal Prolapse?

Rectal prolapse is a condition where the rectum, which is the lower part of the large intestine, moves out of its normal position and may protrude through the anus. It occurs when the supporting muscles, tissues, and ligaments around the rectum become weakened or stretched.

Rectal prolapse can range from mild cases where the rectum only moves slightly during bowel movements to more advanced cases where the rectum remains outside the anus and may require medical intervention.

The condition is different from piles (haemorrhoids), although both may cause discomfort, bleeding, or a lump-like sensation.

Types of Rectal Prolapse

Rectal prolapse is generally classified into three types:

Complete Rectal Prolapse

In complete rectal prolapse, all layers of the rectal wall protrude outside the anus. This is usually more noticeable and may require surgical management.

Partial or Mucosal Prolapse

Only the inner lining of the rectum protrudes through the anal opening. It may sometimes be confused with haemorrhoids.

Internal Rectal Prolapse

The rectum folds inward but does not come outside the anus. It may cause difficulty passing stools or a sensation of incomplete bowel evacuation.

How Does Chronic Straining Lead to Rectal Prolapse?

Chronic straining is one of the important factors associated with rectal prolapse. When a person repeatedly pushes hard during bowel movements, increased pressure is created inside the abdomen and pelvic region.

Over time, this repeated pressure may weaken the structures that support the rectum.

Common situations that may contribute include:

  • Long-term constipation
  • Frequent hard stools
  • Spending excessive time on the toilet
  • Delaying the urge to pass stools
  • Chronic coughing or conditions that increase abdominal pressure
  • Weakening of pelvic floor muscles

The relationship between constipation and rectal prolapse can become a cycle. Straining may worsen rectal support problems, while rectal prolapse itself may make bowel movements more difficult, leading to further straining.

Breaking the Cycle: Managing the Causes Behind Rectal Prolapse

Treating rectal prolapse involves more than addressing the visible symptoms. Doctors usually evaluate the underlying causes, bowel habits, and severity of the condition before recommending treatment.

Improve Bowel Habits

Healthy bowel habits can reduce unnecessary pressure on the rectum.

Helpful practices include:

  • Avoiding prolonged sitting on the toilet
  • Responding to the urge to pass stools
  • Avoiding excessive pushing during bowel movements
  • Maintaining a consistent toilet routine

Manage Constipation Effectively

Chronic constipation management plays an important role in preventing worsening symptoms.

Lifestyle measures may include:

  • Increasing fibre intake through fruits, vegetables, and whole grains
  • Drinking adequate fluids
  • Staying physically active
  • Following medical advice regarding stool softeners or medications when required

Strengthen Pelvic Floor Muscles

The pelvic floor muscles provide support to organs in the lower abdomen, including the rectum. Weakness in these muscles may contribute to prolapse.

Pelvic floor exercises and specialised therapy may be recommended for selected patients.

Common Symptoms of Rectal Prolapse

Symptoms can vary depending on the severity of the condition. Common signs include:

  • A bulge or tissue coming out from the anus during bowel movements
  • Feeling of incomplete bowel evacuation
  • Difficulty controlling bowel movements
  • Mucus discharge
  • Rectal discomfort or pressure
  • Bleeding from the rectal area
  • Difficulty passing stools
  • Irritation around the anal region

Some people may notice that the protruding tissue goes back inside after bowel movements, while others may need to manually push it back.

Ignoring symptoms for a long time may allow the condition to progress, making evaluation more important.

Rectal Prolapse vs Piles: Understanding the Difference

Many people confuse rectal prolapse with piles because both conditions can cause swelling, bleeding, or discomfort around the anus.

However, they are different conditions.

A proper examination by a colorectal specialist helps identify the exact condition and appropriate treatment plan.

When Should You Consult a Doctor for Rectal Prolapse?

Early medical evaluation can help prevent complications and improve treatment outcomes.

You should consider consulting a specialist if you experience:

  • A recurring bulge from the anus
  • Difficulty completing bowel movements
  • Persistent constipation with excessive straining
  • Rectal bleeding
  • Loss of bowel control
  • Increasing discomfort while sitting or walking

A doctor may perform a physical examination and recommend additional tests if required to understand the severity and cause.

Treatment Options for Rectal Prolapse

The treatment approach depends on factors such as the patient’s age, symptoms, severity of prolapse, overall health, and bowel function.

Conservative Management

Mild cases may be managed with:

  • Dietary changes
  • Constipation management
  • Pelvic floor exercises
  • Lifestyle modifications

These approaches may help improve bowel function but may not correct advanced prolapse.

Surgical Treatment

For persistent or advanced rectal prolapse, surgery may be recommended. The goal is to restore normal rectal position and improve symptoms.

Different surgical approaches may be considered depending on individual needs, including procedures performed through the abdomen or through the perineal region.

A colorectal specialist evaluates the condition and recommends the most suitable option.

If you are experiencing symptoms of rectal prolapse or long-standing bowel difficulties, Chirag Global Hospitals in Bangalore provides specialist evaluation and personalised treatment guidance. Schedule a consultation to understand your condition better.

How to Prevent Rectal Prolapse From Worsening

While some factors contributing to rectal prolapse cannot always be avoided, maintaining healthy bowel habits can reduce pressure on the rectal area and support overall digestive health.

Practical Steps to Reduce Straining

Maintain a Fibre-Rich Diet

Fibre helps soften stools and supports smoother bowel movements. Include:

  • Fruits such as apples, papaya, and berries
  • Vegetables and leafy greens
  • Whole grains
  • Legumes and pulses

A gradual increase in fibre intake is recommended because sudden changes may cause bloating or discomfort.

Stay Hydrated

Adequate water intake helps maintain softer stools and supports regular bowel movements. Dehydration can contribute to harder stools, increasing the need for straining.

Avoid Prolonged Toilet Sitting

Spending extended periods on the toilet can increase pressure around the rectal veins and supporting tissues. Try to avoid using mobile phones or other distractions while using the toilet.

Maintain Regular Physical Activity

Regular movement supports bowel function and may help reduce constipation. Simple activities such as walking can improve digestive health.

How Doctors Diagnose Rectal Prolapse

A proper diagnosis helps determine the severity of rectal prolapse and the most suitable treatment approach.

A specialist may evaluate:

  • Symptoms and bowel habits
  • Medical history
  • Physical examination findings
  • Severity of tissue protrusion

Additional tests may sometimes be recommended, such as:

  • Defecography: A specialised imaging test that evaluates how the rectum functions during bowel movements.
  • Colonoscopy: May be suggested in selected cases to examine the colon and rule out other causes of symptoms.
  • Anorectal manometry: Measures the function and strength of muscles involved in bowel control.

The evaluation helps doctors understand whether symptoms are caused by rectal prolapse, piles, constipation-related problems, or another condition.

Can Rectal Prolapse Be Treated Without Surgery?

The need for surgery depends on the severity of the condition. In early or mild cases, conservative measures may help manage symptoms.

Non-surgical approaches may include:

  • Improving bowel habits
  • Treating constipation
  • Pelvic floor rehabilitation
  • Dietary modifications

However, when rectal prolapse becomes more advanced or causes persistent symptoms, surgical treatment may be considered to restore normal anatomy.

A specialist can guide patients after evaluating their symptoms, lifestyle factors, and overall health.

Why Early Treatment Matters

Many people delay seeking medical advice because symptoms may appear only occasionally in the beginning. However, untreated rectal prolapse may gradually affect daily comfort and bowel function.

Possible concerns associated with prolonged rectal prolapse include:

  • Increased difficulty passing stools
  • Worsening constipation
  • Rectal irritation or bleeding
  • Difficulty controlling bowel movements
  • Reduced quality of life

Getting an evaluation early allows doctors to understand the condition and discuss suitable treatment options before symptoms become more complicated.
